scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: Assign and update in turn: $J$ falls from $76$ to $2.6667$

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: the four panels are four half-steps; dot color is the current cluster, crosses are representatives $\boldsymbol{\theta}_j$, thin lines link points to their representative; the right shows $J$ after each half-step.

scene-u01-pnew1-111.name: text#111
scene-u01-pnew1-111.text: In ③, $B$ switches from orange to blue (glow)

scene-u01-pnew1-131.name: text#131
scene-u01-pnew1-131.text: Assignment moves each point to a closer representative; the mean minimizes within-cluster squared distance. $J\ge0$ never increases, so it stops.

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: Stopping is not optimal: the same four points get stuck at $J=16$ from another start

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: both panels have the same four points; the left splits left/right ($J=1$), the right splits top/bottom ($J=16$), and neither can improve; the right lists ways to avoid bad starts.

scene-u01-pnew2-41.name: text#41
scene-u01-pnew2-41.text: On the right every point is at squared distance $4$ from its representative; neither step changes anything, so the algorithm stops.

scene-u01-pnew2-45.name: text#45
scene-u01-pnew2-45.text: "$k$-means stops, so it finds the best clustering" is wrong: it only guarantees $J$ never increases, and may stop at a local minimum.

scene-u01-pnew2-51.name: text#51
scene-u01-pnew2-51.text: Pick $m$ random data points as the start

scene-u01-pnew2-55.name: text#55
scene-u01-pnew2-55.text: Start from a rough sequential clustering

scene-u01-pnew2-59.name: text#59
scene-u01-pnew2-59.text: Split the data randomly into $m$ parts and use their means

scene-u01-pnew2-63.name: text#63
scene-u01-pnew2-63.text: Run from many starts and keep the smallest $J$

scene-u01-pnew2-66.name: text#66
scene-u01-pnew2-66.text: Why not find the best directly

scene-u01-pnew2-67.name: text#67
scene-u01-pnew2-67.text: Finding the best of all partitions is NP-hard; simulated annealing or genetic algorithms can in theory reach the global minimum, but are very expensive.

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: Unequal sizes mislead it: splitting the big group gives a smaller $J$ than the true clustering

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: the left shows the result reached in $45$ of $50$ runs (one in $5$ points drawn); the bars compare $J$ of three solutions; the right lists four built-in limits.

scene-u01-pnew3-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew3-8.text: Big group of $300$ plus small group of $10$, $m=2$

scene-u01-pnew3-86.name: text#86
scene-u01-pnew3-86.text: Blue: cluster 1, orange: cluster 2; green frame: true small group; crosses: representatives

scene-u01-pnew3-87.name: text#87
scene-u01-pnew3-87.text: The right half of the big group joins the small group (right of the dashed line)

scene-u01-pnew3-104.name: text#104
scene-u01-pnew3-104.text: A wrong $m$ cannot reveal the true structure.

scene-u01-pnew3-109.name: text#109
scene-u01-pnew3-109.text: Outliers must join some cluster and drag its mean away.

scene-u01-pnew3-114.name: text#114
scene-u01-pnew3-114.text: Nominal features have no mean, so they do not fit directly.

scene-u01-pnew3-119.name: text#119
scene-u01-pnew3-119.text: Edge points of a big group are far from its center, so cutting them off saves much squared distance.

scene-u01-pnew3-122.name: text#122
scene-u01-pnew3-122.text: Not a bug: a preference built into $J$

scene-u01-pnew3-123.name: text#123
scene-u01-pnew3-123.text: The true clustering has $J=911.7$ and the split one $J\approx890.6$, smaller; the algorithm lowered $J$ correctly, but $J$ prefers splitting big groups.
